verdict.rationale: Snowflake's docs explain the core cost model (credit-based virtual warehouses, doubling costs per size tier, resource monitors to cap spend, cost-anomaly alerts, and pricing tiers) which in principle lets an engineer approximate a bill [snowflake-docs-36,40,43,53,60,42,49]. But hands-on community accounts concretely contradict easy bill estimation: one user reports costs 'could balloon pretty fast' even in a small trial and needing manual safeguards like XSMALL-only warehouses [snowflake-comm-1], and another notes Snowflake lacks query-level cost attribution and built-in recommendations, making it hard to forecast or control spend without extra tooling [snowflake-comm-7]. Missing for 10: a first-party cost calculator/estimator tool, documented per-query cost attribution, and independent case studies showing accurate pre-commitment bill forecasts.
